2609.15851.title: Learning to Coach for Experiential Learning
2609.15851.paper_summary: Language models can learn from experience, but raw solution trajectories are often too long and noisy to provide effective guidance. In this work, we propose Learning to Coach (L2C), a framework that trains a dedicated LLM-as-a-Coach to extract actionable experiential knowledge from an actor model's previous trajectory. The actor remains frozen, while the LLM-as-a-Coach is trained to maximize a reward given by the correctness of the actor's guided response. We study two such rewards: a same-instance reward, which improves subsequent responses on the original problem, and a cross-instance reward, which elicits knowledge that transfers to other instances. Across mathematical reasoning and interactive text-games, L2C consistently outperforms self-refinement and an untrained LLM-as-a-Coach. Running experiential learning for more iterations further improves accuracy and uses additional inference compute more effectively than enlarging the actor's decoding budget. The trained LLM-as-a-Coach also transfers to out-of-distribution tasks and adapts its guidance to the specific actor it coaches.
2609.15851.paper_summary_zh: 語言模型可以從經驗中學習，但原始解決方案的軌跡往往過長且噪音過大，無法提供有效的指導。 在這項工作中，我們提出了學習輔導（Learning to Coach, L2C），這是一個訓練專用的 LLM-as-a-Coach 框架，旨在從演員模型的先前軌跡中提取可行的經驗知識。 演員保持靜止，而 LLM-as-a-Coach 則被訓練以最大化由演員引導的回應的正確性所給予的獎勵。 我們研究了兩種獎勵：同一實例獎勵，這改善了原始問題的後續回應，以及跨實例獎勵，這引發了可轉移到其他實例的知識。 在數學推理和互動文本遊戲中，L2C 始終優於自我精煉和未經訓練的 LLM-as-a-Coach。 進行更多迭代的經驗學習進一步提高了準確性，並比擴大演員的解碼預算更有效地使用額外的推理計算。 訓練過的 LLM-as-a-Coach 也能轉移到分佈外的任務，並根據其輔導的特定演員調整指導。
